items.summary: Energiaministerit kokoontuvat Luxemburgiin keskustelemaan verkkomaksuja koskevasta asetusehdotuksesta, jonka tarkoituksena on varmistaa, että sähkölaskuissa otetaan huomioon tulevaisuuden vaatimukset EU:ssa. He käsittelevät myös energiaturvallisuutta lyhyellä ja pidemmällä aikavälillä sekä vuoden 2030 jälkeisen kehyksen mahdollisia energiatavoitteita.

items.title: WordPress 7.1.4
items.summary: Classification: Critical, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: None, CVEs: , Summary: This security release features fixes for multiple issues. Because this is a security release, it is recommended that you update your sites immediately. As a courtesy, the security fixes were backported to all branches eligible to receive security fixes (currently through 4.7). As a reminder, only the most recent version of WordPress is actively supported. The backports are in progress and will ship as they become ready. WordPress 7.2 Beta 3 has also been released, containing all applicable fixes. Security updates included in this release The security team would like to thank the following people and organizations for responsibly reporting vulnerabilities, and allowing them to be fixed in this release: A weakness in the WordPress upgrade process which can lead to remote code execution during the upgrade window, reported by Umut Bayram. A stored XSS with specially crafted block markup, reported by Rafie Muhammad (Awesome Motive, Inc.). Privacy Data Removal Requests can be created in a way that leads to stored XSS, reported by Anthropic. Multiple stored XSS issues in the Interactivity API independently discovered by AnC and DatNLQ from VietSunshine Cyber Security, rekter0 and Anas cherni, Marcel Karlsson (whoismarcel), and Weston Ruter, Jon Surrell, Alex Concha, and Luis Herranz of the WordPress Security Team. A stored denial of service issue in the Interactivity API, reported by Jon Surrell of the WordPress Security Team. A stored XSS in Customizer selective refresh, reported by Rafie Muhammad (Awesome Motive, Inc.). A Stored XSS in the Categories block reported by Ben Bidner of the WordPress Security Team. Specially crafted User Logins can lead to a stored XSS reported by Anthropic. Unpublished customizer changesets can be discovered by unauthenticated users, reported by Antonio Lorensius Silaban. A Stored XSS in Playlist and image blocks, reported by Ben Bidner of the WordPress Security Team. Stored XSS in core/comments-pagination-next and core/comments-pagination-previous blocks, reported by Alex Concha of the WordPress Security Team. Notes can be read by privileged users that lack access to edit the post the note is attached to, reported by Ramon of the WordPress Security Team. An update to the bundled root certificates due to the eMudhra revocation.

items.title: Commerce Core - Highly critical - Access bypass - SA-CONTRIB-2026-254
items.summary: Classification: Critical, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Functional, CVSSv3.1: None, CVEs: CVE-2026-118539, Summary: Project: Commerce Core Project machine name: commerce Date: 2026-October-28 Security risk: Highly critical 21 ∕ 25 AC:None/A:None/CI:Some/II:Some/E:Exploit/TD:All Vulnerability: Access bypass Affected versions: <2.41 || >=3.0.0 <3.3.13 CVE IDs: CVE-2026-118539 This module enables you to sell goods and services to customers through an included shopping cart and checkout form or through decoupled applications via APIs. The module doesn't sufficiently protect certain routes and entity fields, leading to an access bypass that may financially impact the vendor. This vulnerability is being actively exploited in the wild. Solution: Install the latest version: If you use version 3.x, upgrade to Commerce Core 3.3.13. If you use an earlier version, upgrade to Commerce Core 8.x-2.41. See also: https://www.drupal.org/security

Vulnerability: Access bypass
Affected versions: <2.41 || >=3.0.0 <3.3.13
CVE IDs: CVE-2026-118539

This module enables you to sell goods and services to customers through an included shopping cart and checkout form or through decoupled applications via APIs.

The module doesn't sufficiently protect certain routes and entity fields, leading to an access bypass that may financially impact the vendor.

This vulnerability is being actively exploited in the wild.

Solution: Install the latest version:

If you use version 3.x, upgrade to Commerce Core 3.3.13.
If you use an earlier version, upgrade to Commerce Core 8.x-2.41. See also: https://www.drupal.org/security

items.title: Cisco Advance Notification for Publication of November 4, 2026, Security Advisories
items.summary: Classification: Low, Solution: Not Defined, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: None, CVEs: , Summary: On November 4, 2026, the Cisco Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) will publish advisories to disclose security vulnerability information along with fixed software releases for the following Cisco products: Identity Services Engine (ISE) UCS Central Software Unified Communications Manager To remediate vulnerabilities to be disclosed on November 4, 2026, Cisco strongly recommends that customers upgrade to the fixed software indicated in the advisories. Important: The Cisco PSIRT does not plan to publish any more security hardening advisories to disclose security vulnerability information for the remainder of calendar year 2026. The next planned publication of advisories for security-hardened releases will be January 20, 2027.

items.title: 2026-10 Reference Advisory: Status of PHP2Shell vulnerabilities on Juniper Products (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619)
items.summary: Classification: Critical, Solution: Workaround, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv4.0: 9.3, CVEs: CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619, Summary: The HPE Juniper Networking PSIRT is aware of the two PHP vulnerabilities leading to remote code execution, known as "PHP2Shell", and being tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. RCE via OOM corruption, CVE-2026-109618: out-of-memory handling can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Request cleanup may then treat the invalid data as valid. RCE via stale global state, CVE-2026-109619: request-owned internal state can survive after its backing memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may use that stale state before normal initialization resets it. Below is the current status of Juniper Networking products potentially impacted by the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities: Junos OS: Junos OS is vulnerable to CVE-2026-109618 but not exploitable. The pre-auth out-of-memory issue is reachable but harmless. Junos OS is not affected by CVE-2026-109619. SRX Series: SRX does not use PHP starting with 25.2R1. For earlier versions, Junos OS is vulnerable but not exploitable (see above). Junos OS Evolved (EVO): Not Vulnerable. Session Smart Router: Not Vulnerable. Mist: The following HPE Mist Networking products are not impacted: Mist Cloud Wireless Assurance Wired Assurance Location Services Access Assurance Premium Analytics Mist Access Points Mist Edge WAN Automation: The following HPE WAN Management Software products are not impacted: Routing Director Routing Assurance Routing Active Testing Paragon Insights (formerly Paragon Automation) Paragon Pathfinder/Planner (formerly NorthStar Controller) Junos Space: Not Vulnerable. Apstra: Not Vulnerable. Corero: The Corero SmartWall ONE platform is not vulnerable. Other products not listed above are still under investigation. Juniper SIRT is not aware of any malicious exploitation of this vulnerability. These issues were discovered by a third-party upstream provider. Solution Software releases will be updated to resolve this issue and made available on the Customer Support Downloads site. This issue is being tracked as 1959788, 1990005, 1990031, 1990051 and 1990294 which are visible on the Customer Support website. Note: Juniper SIRT's policy is not to evaluate releases that are beyond End of Engineering (EOE) or End of Life (EOL). Workaround For most products, disable web access or limit access to trusted hosts and administrators.

items.title: Microsoft urges Entra ID admins to migrate users to passkeys
items.summary: Microsoft again asked Entra ID administrators to migrate users to phishing-resistant methods to avoid sign-in disruptions before it retires SMS and voice authentication in February 2027. This retirement process applies only to Microsoft Entra ID workforce tenant authentication scenarios and not to Azure AD B2C or Microsoft Entra External ID customer identity scenarios. Before Microsoft retires SMS and voice authentication, admins should ensure all users in their organizations use a phishing-resistant method, since they will no longer be able to use them to complete multifactor authentication and log in to their accounts.

items.title: Hackers now scanning systems for recently-patched Oracle flaw
items.summary: Attackers have begun probing the Internet for systems unpatched against a recently disclosed critical Oracle E-Business Suite (EBS) vulnerability. Discovered in a core component of EBS's Application Object Library and tracked as CVE-2026-101767, this flaw lets unauthenticated threat actors with HTTP network access take over vulnerable systems in low-complexity attacks. Oracle released security updates to address the issue in its October 2026 Critical Security Patch Update on October 20 and urged customers to patch their systems immediately.

items.title: 123 Reg discloses 'AI cyberattack' on customer data, suspects China nexus
items.summary: UK domain registrar 123 Reg says it was the victim of an “AI-driven cyberattack” that exposed customer data. Customers began receiving their notification emails this week, informing them that their contact information, "related customer relationship data," company VAT numbers, and "product information from an application programming interface (API)" were compromised. A company spokesperson elaborated, saying this means that names, phone numbers, countries, language and currency preferences, account creation dates, the products on the account, and marketing preferences were affected. 123 Reg described the September 18 intrusion as "the first known AI-driven cyberattack against our company," and told The Register that early signs point toward a China-nexus attacker. "Our investigation identified IP addresses that we assessed to be the core attacker infrastructure, which were hosted in China and Singapore, indicating a strong Chinese nexus," the spokesperson said. "Our investigation further identified AI cyberattack 'skills' hosted on Chinese infrastructure, including copies of skills open sourced by Anthropic and several other AI exploitation frameworks and scripts." They went on to say that many of the artefacts left behind led 123 Reg to suspect that a Chinese state-sponsored group, known for abusing Claude Code in attacks against at least 30 organizations, could be behind the break-in.

items.title: Uusi digitaalisen turvallisuuden yhteistyöryhmä vahvistamaan huoltovarmuuden kehittämistä
items.summary: Huoltovarmuuskeskus vahvistaa digitaalisen yhteiskunnan varautumisen kehittämistä uudella, eri toimialojen asiantuntijoista koostuvalla yhteistyöryhmällä. Digitaalisen turvallisuuden neuvottelukunta on neuvoa-antava yhteistyöfoorumi. Sen jäseninä on eri toimialojen yritysten digitaalisen turvallisuuden asiantuntijoita. Neuvottelukunta keskittyy eri toimialojen yhteisiin teemoihin, kuten kvanttilaskennan tietoturvavaikutuksiin, tekoälyn riskeihin ja digitaaliseen suvereniteettiin. Lisäksi se vauhdittaa kyberturvallisuuden vahvistamista eri toimialoilla ja vie eteenpäin toimenpiteitä kyberkypsyyden tason nostamiseksi yrityksissä. Neuvottelukunnan tavoitteena on kasvattaa ymmärrystä digitalisaation, tekoälyn ja muiden nousevien teknologioiden vaikutuksista digitaaliseen turvallisuuteen ja varautumiseen sekä kehittää huoltovarmuusorganisaation eli yritysten ja viranomaisten yhteistyöverkostojen varautumista ajankohtaisiin teknologisiin aiheisiin. Lisäksi se muodostaa yhteistä tilannekuvaa, auttaa kohdistamaan toimenpiteitä vaikuttavasti ja pyrkii vahvistamaan yritysten ymmärrystä, tahtoa ja kykyä toimia digitaalisen huoltovarmuuden hyväksi.

Yhtiö julkaisi tammikuussa AWS European Sovereign Cloud -pilvipalvelun. Palvelu on tarkoitettu eurooppalaisille asiakkaille, jotka haluavat pitää tietonsa EU:n sisällä. items.title: Pre-boot RCE in EDK II PXE driver (Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware)
items.summary: Classification: Critical, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: 9.5, CVEs: CVE-2026-97631, Summary: The vulnerability, with a severity rating of 9.5 out of 10, resides in the TianoCore EDK II, an open source codebase that hardware makers and cloud providers use to create the UEFI firmware that runs during the boot-up sequence. Last year, a representative of the UEFI Forum called EDK2 the “preeminent solution / implementation of the UEFI specifications.” Virtually all UEFI suppliers (sometimes still called IBVs or independent BIOS vendors), including AMI, Insyde, and Phoenix, use the reference code extensively. Project Mu, Microsoft’s hardened EDK2 fork, used the code containing the vulnerable component as well. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-97631, is a memory-corruption flaw in an ICMP component that attackers can exploit to execute malicious code that runs before the operating system and firmware can implement defenses like Secure Boot, which establishes a chain of trust for all code, including the Trusted Platform Module (TPM), loaded during boot. While final payloads delivered by CVE-2026-97631 have no persistence—meaning they run only once—they can give attackers a wide opening to install other payloads that also run each time early in the boot process. While a machine is PXE-booting over IPv4 or IPv6, an unauthenticated network attacker who can deliver ICMP error messages to it can corrupt DXE-phase memory and execute arbitrary code before the operating system loads, before Secure Boot or measured boot has verified or measured any OS component. See also: https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/10/code-execution-flaw-in-uefi-firmware-threatens-most-servers-on-planet-earth/

items.title: CyberStrikeAI Uses 44 AI Agents to Automate Hacking Operations Against Japan Targets
items.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of three cyber attacks targeting organizations in Japan in which artificial intelligence (AI) was a key element, either in the driving seat or to assist a human operator. TrendAI, which analyzed three exposed server environments used by threat actors to conduct the malicious cyber operations, described them as distinct from previously published attacks that have leveraged ARTEX, an autonomous AI penetration testing framework, to single out entities in South Korea and Japan. "These environments held reconnaissance and attack tools, scripts, target lists, results, logs, and command histories," security researchers Bakuei Matsukawa and Joseph C Chen said. "They ranged from workspaces used largely by hand by skilled operators to AI-agent platforms that automated the entire workflow, including command and control."

items.title: UNM Health ransomware attack disrupts patient care, surgeries
items.summary: The University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center disclosed a cyberattack that caused system outages and disrupted patient care and academic activities. On Monday, UNM Health, the university’s healthcare provider, began temporarily limiting new patient admissions, diverting ambulances to nearby hospitals, and suspending outpatient surgeries and appointments. In an update on the incident, UNM said UNM Hospital and Sandoval Regional Medical Center remain open, and all clinics will resume scheduled appointments and procedures starting today, Tuesday, October 27.

items.title: Hackers hijack Convertr analytics script to steal payment card data
items.summary: A credit card skimming group reportedly compromised a shared analytics script used by e-commerce platform Convertr to steal shoppers’ payment data during checkout. The campaign was identified on October 24 and has been attributed to a Brazilian gang, active since at least July 2024, that focuses on infecting online stores running Magento, OpenCart, and WooCommerce platforms. Convertr is a Brazilian e-commerce platform that powers online stores and checkout systems for dozens of major fashion brands in the country, handling R$2 billion ($370M) in sales.
